title: Twisted bilayer graphene turns superconducting at a magic angle

passages: Jun Ye Wolf Prize Laureate in Physics 2026 Jun Ye Affiliation at the time of the award: National Institute of Standards & Technology (NIST), University of Colorado, USA Award citation: “For transformative, widely applicable advances in the control of ultracold atomic systems”.
Bloch transformed ultracold atoms into a powerful platform for simulating and investigating complex quantum systems, helping to establish quantum simulation as a major field of modern physics.

Ye has led the development of the world’s most accurate and stable optical atomic clocks, enabling measurements of time and frequency at extraordinary levels of precision and opening new possibilities for testing fundamental physics.

Together, their achievements exemplify a defining transition in modern physics: from observing the quantum world to controlling, measuring, and harnessing it for scientific discovery and emerging technologies.
A gifted high-school physics teacher changed his direction, encouraging him to enter a national physics competition—an experience that awakened his fascination with experimental physics.

His research has opened new possibilities for tests of fundamental physics, including the most sensitive search for the electron’s electric dipole moment, relativistic geodesy, and searches for variations in fundamental constants.
